_about: Common operations side by side, with the defaults that make them differ. Used by tools/translate.py idioms and by the translation agents as a starting point; every row is checked against the documentation of the versions in use before it is relied on.

idioms.sas: proc import datafile="f.csv" out=d dbms=csv replace; run;
idioms.note: Type guessing differs: check that codes with leading zeros, dates and missing-value markers are read the same way.

idioms.eviews: equation eq.ls y c x1 x2
idioms.sas: proc reg data=d; model y = x1 x2; run;
idioms.note: EViews needs the constant c; statsmodels arrays (not formulas) need add_constant.

idioms.r: coeftest(m, vcov = vcovHC(m, type = "HC1"))  # vcovHC defaults to HC3
idioms.eviews: eq.ls(cov=white) y c x  # check the degrees-of-freedom option
idioms.sas: proc reg; model y = x / hcc hccmethod=1; run;
idioms.note: Name the HC variant explicitly in every language; defaults differ (Stata HC1, R sandwich HC3).

idioms.r: vcovCL(m, cluster = ~id, type = "HC1")  # or fixest::feols(..., cluster = ~id)
idioms.eviews: panel workfile: eq.ls(cov=perwhite) y c x  # robust to correlation within each cross-section unit; check the manual
idioms.sas: proc surveyreg; cluster id; model y = x; run;
idioms.note: Small-sample factors differ by package and by model (pooled OLS against fixed effects); compare standard errors, not only coefficients.

idioms.task: Panel regression with unit fixed effects
idioms.stata:
xtset id year
xtreg y x, fe
idioms.eviews: panel workfile: equation eq.ls(cx=f) y c x
idioms.sas: proc panel; id id year; model y = x / fixone; run;
idioms.note: xtreg, fe reports a constant and uses its own degrees of freedom; areg and dummy-variable OLS give the same slopes with different standard errors.

idioms.stata: L.x  # after xtset or tsset; respects gaps
idioms.r: dplyr::lag(x) within group_by(id)  # positional, ignores gaps
idioms.sas: lag(x)  # a queue; wrong inside IF statements
idioms.note: If the time index has gaps, a positional lag takes the wrong period. Reindex to a complete calendar first or lag by date.

idioms.python: x.diff()  # same length, first value NaN
idioms.sas: dif(x)
idioms.note: Length changes shift alignment with other series.

idioms.stata: x > 5 is true when x is missing
idioms.r: x > 5 is NA when x is NA; subset() and which() drop it
idioms.python: x > 5 is False when x is NaN
idioms.matlab: x > 5 is false when x is NaN
idioms.eviews: NA in a comparison gives NA; the observation is dropped from the sample
idioms.julia: x > 5 is missing when x is missing
idioms.sas: x > 5 is false when x is missing (missing is the smallest value)
idioms.note: Translate 'if x > 5' from Stata as 'x > 5 and x is not missing' unless the source intended to include missing values.

idioms.python: d.x.mean()  # pandas skips NaN; np.mean does not
idioms.eviews: @mean(x)  # over the current sample, skipping NA
idioms.sas: proc means; var x; run;  # skips missing

idioms.python: d.x.std()  # pandas n-1; np.std(x) is n unless ddof=1
idioms.sas: proc means std; run;  # n-1 (VARDEF=DF)
idioms.note: NumPy is the exception: np.std and np.var default to ddof=0.

idioms.sas: proc univariate  # PCTLDEF=5 = R type 2
idioms.note: Set the definition explicitly in the target (R type =, NumPy method =) to match the source.

idioms.r: aggregate(y ~ g, data = d, FUN = mean)
idioms.sas: proc means nway noprint; class g; var y; output out=o mean=; run;
idioms.note: Check how each handles missing values in y and in the group variable (pandas drops NaN groups unless dropna=False).

idioms.task: Group statistic kept on every row
idioms.r: d$m <- ave(d$y, d$g)  # ave does not skip NA
idioms.matlab: [G, ~] = findgroups(T.g); m = splitapply(@mean, T.y, G); T.m = m(G);
idioms.sas: proc sql; create table d2 as select *, mean(y) as m from d group by g; quit;

idioms.r: merge(a, b, by = c("id", "year"), all = TRUE)
idioms.eviews: copy or link series between pages by id and date
idioms.sas: data m; merge a b; by id year; run;  # both sorted first
idioms.note: Check the match type (1:1, m:1) and the unmatched rows explicitly; SAS MERGE does not form a Cartesian product for many-to-many keys.

idioms.julia: sort(d, [:id, :year])  # stable by default for DataFrames
idioms.sas: proc sort data=d; by id year; run;  # EQUALS is the default
idioms.note: Any result that depends on the order of tied rows (first observation, cumulative sums) needs a stable sort and a full key.

idioms.python: round(x) or np.round(x)  # half to even
idioms.julia: round(x)  # half to even; RoundNearestTiesAway for the other rule
idioms.sas: round(x)  # half away from zero
idioms.note: Excel ROUND rounds half away from zero but VBA Round rounds half to even.

idioms.sas: log(x)
idioms.note: Excel LOG is base 10; LN is the natural logarithm.

idioms.stata: tsfilter hp c = y, smooth(1600) trend(t)
idioms.matlab: [trend, cycle] = hpfilter(y, Smoothing=1600)  # output order depends on release
idioms.sas: proc ucm or proc expand; check the method
idioms.note: Outputs come back in different orders (cycle first in statsmodels) and default lambdas depend on frequency in EViews.

idioms.r: arima(y, order = c(1, 0, 0), method = "ML")  # default is CSS-ML
idioms.eviews: equation eq.ls y c ar(1)  # check the estimation method option
idioms.sas: proc arima; identify var=y; estimate p=1 method=ml; run;
idioms.note: Exact against conditional likelihood and the treatment of the mean give different estimates in short samples.

idioms.sas: proc varmax; model y1 y2 / p=2; run;
idioms.note: Residual covariance divisors (T or T-k), the Cholesky ordering and the IRF normalization (one standard deviation or unit) differ.

idioms.r: glm(y ~ x, family = binomial, data = d)
idioms.sas: proc logistic descending; model y = x; run;  # without DESCENDING it models y = 0

idioms.stata: i.g  # base is the lowest value
idioms.r: factor(g)  # base is the first level
idioms.python: C(g)  # base is the first sorted level; C(g, Treatment(reference=...)) to set it
idioms.matlab: categorical(g)  # base is the first category
idioms.sas: class g / param=ref ref=first;  # default reference is the last level
idioms.note: Set the base level explicitly; defaults differ (SAS uses the last level).

idioms.task: Random uniform draws with a seed
idioms.sas: call streaminit(1); u = rand("uniform");
idioms.note: The same seed gives different draws in every language. Export the source draws and read them, or compare distributions.

idioms.r: solve(A, b)  # qr.solve for least squares
idioms.python: np.linalg.solve(A, b)  # np.linalg.lstsq for least squares
idioms.matlab: x = A \ b;  # least squares when A is not square
idioms.sas: proc iml; x = solve(A, b); quit;

idioms.task: Reshape a vector into a matrix
idioms.stata: mata: rowshape(x, m)  # row by row
idioms.r: matrix(x, nrow = m)  # column by column
idioms.python: x.reshape(m, n, order="F")  # to match MATLAB, R, Julia and Fortran
idioms.matlab: reshape(x, m, n)  # column by column
idioms.julia: reshape(x, m, n)  # column by column
idioms.sas: proc iml; shape(x, m)  # row by row
idioms.note: Storage order is the most common silent error when moving numerical code into Python or C.

idioms.python: scipy.optimize.minimize(f, x0)  # BFGS by default without bounds
idioms.sas: proc nlp or proc optmodel
idioms.note: Compare the optimum and the objective value, not the iteration path; record the method and tolerances.

idioms.eviews: date numbers are days since 1 January 0001 (check @dateval)
idioms.julia: Date: Rata Die days since 1 January 0001
idioms.sas: days since 1 January 1960
idioms.note: Excel serial dates start on 30 December 1899 and include a non-existent 29 February 1900.

idioms.sas: proc export data=t outfile="output/<run-id>/t.csv" dbms=csv replace; run;
idioms.note: Write full precision (not display formats) in both source and target runs, so tools/translate.py compare can check them.
